note: True/false pool for Circuit Breaker. Weighted toward the things people get wrong, especially the 2026 rule changes.

statements.s: NEPSE trades Sunday to Thursday.
statements.why: Monday to Friday since April 2026. It ran Sunday–Thursday for its entire prior history, which is why almost every guide online still says so.

statements.s: NEPSE trades Monday to Friday.
statements.why: Changed in April 2026, following the shift in government office days.

statements.s: You can place a market order on NEPSE.
statements.why: Every NEPSE order is a limit order. You must always name a price.

statements.s: A stock can move 15% in one day.
statements.why: The daily circuit rose from ±10% to ±15% of the previous close, effective 21 April 2026.

statements.s: The daily price limit for a single stock is ±10%.
statements.why: It was raised to ±15% on 21 April 2026.

statements.s: Short-term capital gains tax on shares is 7.5% for individuals.
statements.why: It rose to 10% on 17 July 2026. The 7.5% figure is now the long-term rate.

statements.s: Short-term capital gains tax on shares is 10% for individuals.
statements.why: Raised from 7.5% on 17 July 2026 (1 Shrawan 2083).

statements.s: Long-term capital gains tax for individuals is 7.5%.
statements.why: Raised from 5% on 17 July 2026, and it applies to holdings of more than 365 days.

statements.s: Institutional capital gains tax is 10%, regardless of holding period.
statements.why: It did not change in July 2026, and there is no long-term rate for institutions.

statements.s: You can sell shares the same day you buy them.
statements.why: T+2 settlement makes intraday impossible — you cannot sell what has not reached your Demat.

statements.s: Bonus shares are taxed when you receive them.
statements.why: Not a taxable event at issue. They reduce your WACC, so the tax arrives later when you sell.

statements.s: DP charge is Rs. 25 per trade.
statements.why: It is Rs. 25 per company per settlement date. Two buys of the same stock on one day cost Rs. 25 once.

statements.s: DP charge is Rs. 25 per company per settlement date.
statements.why: Flat, which makes it punishing on small trades — a Rs. 1,000 trade pays 2.5% in DP charge alone.

statements.s: Orders can now be placed outside market hours.
statements.why: Since April 2026 orders can be entered round the clock. They queue; execution is only 11:00–15:00.

statements.s: Orders placed at midnight execute immediately.
statements.why: They queue. Execution happens only during the 11:00–15:00 session.

statements.s: Settlement on NEPSE is T+2 in calendar days.
statements.why: T+2 in trading days. A Thursday sale settles on Monday.

statements.s: A sale executed on Thursday settles on Monday.
statements.why: T+2 counts trading days, and the market is closed Saturday and Sunday.

statements.s: You must authorise EDIS in MeroShare when you sell.
statements.why: On T+1. Without it the shares are never delivered and the trade goes to auction settlement.

statements.s: Your broker can authorise EDIS on your behalf.
statements.why: Only you can release shares from your own Demat account. That is the whole point of the custody separation.

statements.s: Short selling is available on NEPSE.
statements.why: There is no short selling, no options and no futures. NEPSE is a cash equity market.

statements.s: There are no exchange-traded options on NEPSE.
statements.why: No derivatives of any kind. Cash equity only.

statements.s: The exchange lends you money to buy shares on margin.
statements.why: NEPSE offers no leverage. Funds must clear into your broker's account before you buy.

statements.s: Broker commission is negotiable if you trade often.
statements.why: The five slabs are regulated, not commercial. Your broker cannot discount them.

statements.s: Broker commission runs on five slabs from 0.36% down to 0.24%.
statements.why: And it is applied to the whole transaction amount, not marginally.

statements.s: Commission slabs are marginal, like income tax bands.
statements.why: They apply to the whole amount. Crossing a boundary can lower your total commission.

statements.s: A Rs. 5,10,000 trade can cost less commission than a Rs. 4,90,000 trade.
statements.why: Rs. 1,581 versus Rs. 1,617 — because slabs are not marginal.

statements.s: The SEBON fee on equity trades is 0.015%.
statements.why: Corporate debentures are 0.010% and government bonds 0.005%.

statements.s: Capital gains tax on listed shares is filed annually with your return.
statements.why: It is withheld at source during settlement and is a final tax.

statements.s: Capital gains tax on listed shares is a final tax.
statements.why: Which also means losses on listed shares generally cannot offset your other income.

statements.s: A holding of exactly 365 days qualifies for the long-term CGT rate.
statements.why: The threshold is more than 365 days. Exactly 365 is short-term.

statements.s: Cash dividends for individuals are taxed at 5%, deducted at source.
statements.why: Separate from capital gains tax, and not part of the CGT calculation.

statements.s: The index circuit breaker halts trading for 15 minutes on a 5% move in the first two hours.
statements.why: Level 1 of the two-tier system introduced on 21 April 2026.

statements.s: An 8% index move closes the market for the day.
statements.why: Level 2, at any time of day, since 21 April 2026.

statements.s: The index circuit breaker has three tiers.
statements.why: Simplified to two tiers on 21 April 2026.

statements.s: The order price band is ±3% of the last traded price.
statements.why: Relaxed from ±2% in 2026. It moves as the stock moves.

statements.s: The order price band and the daily circuit use the same reference price.
statements.why: The band is ±3% of the LTP; the circuit is ±15% of the previous close.

statements.s: The pre-open price band is ±5% of the previous close.
statements.why: Raised from ±2% in 2026.

statements.s: In the pre-open session, orders match continuously as they arrive.
statements.why: Orders are collected without matching, then a single equilibrium price is calculated.

statements.s: Matching on NEPSE is by price, then by time.
statements.why: Price–time priority. At the same price, whoever arrived first fills first.

statements.s: If two buyers bid the same price, the larger order fills first.
statements.why: Time decides, not size. The earlier order fills first.

statements.s: An unfilled order stays live until you cancel it.
statements.why: NEPSE orders are day orders and expire at the close. There is no good-till-cancelled.

statements.s: Modifying an order's price loses your place in the time queue.
statements.why: A modified order re-enters at the back of the queue for its new price.

statements.s: You can cancel a portion of your order that has already executed.
statements.why: Executed is executed. Only the unfilled remainder can be cancelled.

statements.s: An order that fills across two days incurs two DP charges.
statements.why: Two settlement dates, so Rs. 25 twice. A small argument for orders you expect to fill completely.

statements.s: MeroShare can be used to place buy orders.
statements.why: MeroShare is custody. Orders are placed in TMS, through your broker.

statements.s: TMS is where you apply for an IPO.
statements.why: IPO applications go through MeroShare's My ASBA, not TMS.

statements.s: Your official cost basis for tax is the WACC shown in MeroShare.
statements.why: Not the figure in your broker's TMS portfolio view.

statements.s: You need a Demat account before you can apply for any IPO.
statements.why: C-ASBA runs through MeroShare, which requires a Demat with a DP.

statements.s: C-ASBA debits your bank account when you apply for an IPO.
statements.why: It blocks the funds in your own account. They are debited only if you are allotted.

statements.s: Applying for 100 units instead of 10 improves your IPO allotment odds.
statements.why: The lottery gives every valid application equal probability regardless of size.

statements.s: You may submit more than one IPO application per person per issue.
statements.why: Duplicates are rejected and both applications may be voided.

statements.s: Fixed-price IPOs are priced at the Rs. 100 face value with a minimum of 10 units.
statements.why: Rs. 1,000 minimum, deliberately accessible.

statements.s: The book-building minimum for retail is 10 units.
statements.why: It is 50 units, which meaningfully raises the entry cost for retail.

statements.s: Retail investors get a 10% discount to the institutional price in a book-built issue.
statements.why: Part of the 2026 IPO rules.

statements.s: Mutual fund units have a face value of Rs. 100.
statements.why: Rs. 10, with a minimum application of 100 units.

statements.s: Closed-end mutual funds usually trade below their NAV.
statements.why: A persistent discount, which narrows as maturity approaches.

statements.s: Unexercised rights shares are automatically credited to you.
statements.why: They lapse. You lose value by doing nothing.

statements.s: A bonus issue increases the total value of your holding.
statements.why: More shares, proportionally lower price. You own more pieces of the same pie.

statements.s: A bonus issue lowers your WACC.
statements.why: The same total cost spread across more shares — which raises the taxable gain later.

statements.s: Reported EPS falls after a bonus issue even if profit rose.
statements.why: The share count in the denominator grew. Restate prior EPS by dividing by (1 + bonus ratio).

statements.s: A high P/E in Nepali banking usually means the market expects rapid growth.
statements.why: It usually means earnings collapsed. NICA at 343× had an EPS of Rs. 1.76 and an ROE of 0.88%.

statements.s: P/E is meaningless when EPS is negative.
statements.why: Arithmetically undefined in any useful sense. Laxmi Sunrise reported EPS of −Rs. 2.04.

statements.s: The median P/E of Nepali commercial banks was about 14.92× in Q2 2082/83.
statements.why: Against a range running from 7.67× to 343.16×.

statements.s: A low P/E always means a stock is a bargain.
statements.why: NBL at 7.67× had an ROE of 6.76% — cheap because it earns poorly. Read P/E next to ROE.

statements.s: ROE measures how efficiently a company turns shareholder capital into profit.
statements.why: Net profit as a percentage of shareholders' equity.

statements.s: Rising non-performing loans tend to precede falling bank EPS.
statements.why: By roughly two to four quarters, which is why NPL is worth more than the current P/E.

statements.s: Installed capacity in megawatts tells you a hydropower company's revenue.
statements.why: It is a licence. Plant Load Factor is what actually generates revenue.

statements.s: Most Nepali hydropower projects are run-of-river and therefore seasonal.
statements.why: Which is why you compare Q2 to the same quarter last year, never to Q1.

statements.s: Comparing a hydropower company's Q3 to its Q2 tells you about the business.
statements.why: It tells you about the weather. Compare year-on-year.

statements.s: A hydropower project without a signed PPA still has a clear route to revenue.
statements.why: The Power Purchase Agreement with NEA is the business model. No PPA, no revenue.

statements.s: Hydropower is the largest sector on NEPSE by company count.
statements.why: 91 of 271 companies, or 33.6%.

statements.s: The 19 commercial banks dominate the cap-weighted NEPSE index.
statements.why: Company count is not market weight. When the news says NEPSE rose, it mostly means the banks did.

statements.s: Complaints about a broker go to NEPSE.
statements.why: They go to SEBON, the regulator. NEPSE operates the market and cannot discipline a broker.

statements.s: SEBON approves every IPO prospectus.
statements.why: And publishes them, which is why the objectives-of-the-issue section is worth reading.

statements.s: CDSC holds your shares; your broker does not.
statements.why: The custody separation protects you if a broker fails — and it is why EDIS exists.

statements.s: The NEPSE floorsheet is public.
statements.why: Published daily on nepalstock.com, with buying broker, selling broker, quantity and rate.

statements.s: The floorsheet identifies the individual investor behind each trade.
statements.why: It shows broker numbers. One broker has thousands of clients.

statements.s: The all-time high of the NEPSE index is 3,198.60.
statements.why: Set on 18 August 2021 and not reclaimed in five years.

statements.s: The NEPSE index has recovered its 2021 all-time high.
statements.why: At 2,643.83 it is still about 17.3% below it, five years on.

statements.s: The 2021–2023 drawdown was roughly 50%.
statements.why: 3,198.60 to 1,615 — down 49.5%, needing +98.1% to recover.

statements.s: Recovering a 50% loss requires a 50% gain.
statements.why: It requires 100%. G = L ÷ (1 − L).

statements.s: Recovering a 20% loss requires a 25% gain.
NEPSE offers a stop-loss order type.
statements.why: It does not. Your stop is a decision you execute manually, which makes position size your primary risk control.

statements.s: Position size should be derived from your stop distance.
statements.why: Rupee risk ÷ (entry − stop). Size is never chosen first.

statements.s: Risking 1–2% of your account per trade keeps one mistake from being structural.
statements.why: It keeps you on the flat part of the recovery curve.

statements.s: A 40% win rate cannot be profitable.
statements.why: At 2:1 reward-to-risk, 40% winners produce a positive expectancy.

statements.s: Five Nepali commercial banks make a well-diversified portfolio.
statements.why: They correlate at roughly 0.90. Five names is close to one position.

statements.s: The spread is a fee charged by your broker.
statements.why: It is the gap between bid and ask — the cost of trading immediately, paid to nobody in particular.

statements.s: On thin NEPSE counters the spread can exceed the commission several times over.
statements.why: A 2–3% spread against a 0.33% commission is normal on illiquid hydropower counters.

statements.s: A candlestick pattern on 400 shares traded is a reliable signal.
statements.why: That is one person with a small order, not information.

statements.s: A hammer and a hanging man are drawn identically.
statements.why: Only the preceding trend separates them — a hammer follows a decline, a hanging man an advance.

statements.s: In a bullish engulfing pattern, the second candle's wicks must engulf the first candle's wicks.
statements.why: Only the bodies need to be engulfed. Beginners reject valid signals over this.

statements.s: Up candles are conventionally drawn hollow in this course.
statements.why: So that shape carries the signal too, and meaning is never encoded in colour alone.

statements.s: A doji is a reliable reversal signal on its own.
statements.why: It records indecision. It means something only after an extended trend, and only with confirmation.

statements.s: A candle that closes at the circuit limit tells you buyers and sellers reached agreement.
statements.why: Price stopped because it was not allowed to move, not because anyone agreed.

statements.s: RSI above 70 is a sell signal.
statements.why: Overbought can stay overbought for months. It is a condition, not an instruction.

statements.s: Moving average crossovers work best as confirmation rather than as a trigger.
statements.why: They lag by construction. Using one as a trigger buys the move after it happened.

statements.s: Indicators are less reliable on illiquid counters.
statements.why: Stale prices, gaps and circuit days corrupt the inputs the indicator is computed from.

statements.s: Adding a third momentum indicator to a system that has two makes it more robust.
statements.why: Correlated indicators repeat the same signal and manufacture false confidence.

statements.s: A trend is defined by higher highs and higher lows.
statements.why: And a downtrend by lower highs and lower lows. Anything else is a range.

statements.s: A support level that has held four times is stronger than one that has held twice.
statements.why: Two touches is the minimum for a level and the weakest version of one.

statements.s: A breakout without volume confirmation is as reliable as one with it.
statements.why: Volume is what separates a breakout from a fakeout.

statements.s: A valid breakout on a counter you cannot actually buy is still tradeable.
statements.why: That is the NEPSE liquidity trap. Check average daily turnover before trading any pattern.

statements.s: Round numbers like Rs. 100, 500 and 1,000 carry psychological weight on NEPSE.
statements.why: They manufacture support and resistance through pure anchoring.

statements.s: A tip that names a target price but no scenario in which it fails is a warning sign.
statements.why: The absence of a downside case is the tell.

statements.s: SEBON prohibits coordinated market manipulation.
statements.why: And it is where you report it. Trying to time an exit ahead of the organisers is not a plan.

statements.s: Averaging down reduces your total risk.
statements.why: It lowers your average cost and raises your total exposure at the same time.

statements.s: Loss aversion makes people hold losers and sell winners.
statements.why: A loss feels roughly twice as strong as an equivalent gain.

statements.s: Your buy price is relevant to whether a company is worth holding today.
statements.why: The market does not know your entry. Anchoring to it is Lesson 15.3.

statements.s: Accelerating new-account growth is one of the reliable late-cycle warning signs.
statements.why: It means the last buyers are arriving. So is junk outperforming leaders, and rising leverage.

statements.s: A trade journal needs at least fifteen columns to be useful.
statements.why: Seven. Add an eighth and you will stop filling it in by week three.

statements.s: 'Buy good stocks' is a testable trading rule.
statements.why: Two people reading it would buy different things. A rule needs a number and a source.

statements.s: Break-even is your buy price plus the round-trip cost of getting in and out.
statements.why: Below it there is no gain, so there is no CGT — the one mercy in the arithmetic.

statements.s: A Rs. 1,000 trade needs roughly a 5.8% move just to break even.
statements.why: 5.77%, because the flat Rs. 25 DP charge is 2.5% of the trade on its own.

statements.s: A Rs. 2,30,000 trade needs a larger percentage move to break even than a Rs. 1,000 trade.
statements.why: The opposite: about 0.7% versus 5.77%, entirely because the DP charge is flat.

statements.s: Keeping round-trip friction under about 1% requires positions of roughly Rs. 25,000 or more.
statements.why: Below that, the flat charges dominate.

statements.s: The spread is your first cost, before any commission is charged.
statements.why: You buy at the ask and sell into the bid; the gap is paid before a fee is levied.

statements.s: Nepal Rastra Bank sets minimum paid-up capital for banks.
statements.why: Which is why banks issue so many bonus shares — it raises capital without a cash call.

statements.s: Promoter shares can be sold freely the day a company lists.
statements.why: They carry lock-in periods and trade in a separate segment.

statements.s: Face value of Rs. 100 means a share is worth Rs. 100.
statements.why: It is an accounting convention used for paid-up capital and IPO pricing, not a valuation.

statements.s: A share trading below Rs. 100 is automatically cheap.
statements.why: It usually means the market thinks the company is worth less than the capital put into it.

statements.s: Money you pay for shares in the secondary market reaches the company.
statements.why: It reaches the seller. Only primary-market money funds the business.

statements.s: IPO money funds the company; secondary-market money does not.
statements.why: Which is why the objectives-of-the-issue section of a prospectus matters.

statements.s: Failing to deliver sold shares triggers auction settlement, and the cost lands on you.
statements.why: NEPSE buys the shares in the market to deliver, and charges you the difference plus a penalty.

statements.s: Trading hours are 11:00 to 15:00.
statements.why: With a pre-open session before the open.
